title: Construct sharp two-thirds boxes with distinct factor directions (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with finite exact corroboration: construct rational three-total factorizations on `3ks` lines whose directed sub-anchor box is exactly `2ks`, with `3k` distinct projective directions of multiplicity `s` in each factor and exactly `2s` zeros per row and column. Every canonical tied set has size two. The union of two disjoint ordered nonzero blocks has the same exact maximum.

For `k=4,s=1`, all twelve factor directions are distinct, every row/column has two zeros, and the box is exactly eight. This supplies a sharp family inside the structural restrictions left by [Sagar Thakrar's #3445](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3445). Distinct directions and sparse zeros alone cannot force a strict improvement over the two-thirds box ratio. The universal rational twelve-line lower bound remains open.

```text
N = u v^T,  v^T u = 0
P_t = (I+4tN) P0
Q_t = D (I+4tN)^(-T) D^(-1) Q0
P_t Q_r^T = (I+4(t-r)N)D
```

The new contribution is this anchor-preserving family and its distinct-direction argument. Aaron Wang/navinor retains the #2978 rational core and triangular-rank argument, canonical anchors and directed-box/SG lineage. Sagar Thakrar retains #3445's question and the #3435/#3420/#3409 ordered-block lineage; DreamingOfClouds retains F-star. This contribution is produced by Nick Petalas. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19291872) and [scope update](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19291986). The delivered scope is the first partial sharpness construction. The original universal remainder is still open. Base and last refreshed canonical main: `2485805a6d47f36ea83ddde6327d453ac82d44dc`, priority revision eight. No selected-frontier change or new kappa.

## Evidence

Before: #3445 gives necessary multiplicity/zero-degree conditions and a repeated-core sharp example. After: an explicit family attains the same ratio with all directions distinct and two scalar zeros per row/column at `s=1`. This is construction work; no predecessor scientific suite is audited or replayed.

Locally executed on macOS arm64, CPython 3.12.15, standard library only:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/fstar-distinct-direction-sharpness/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/fstar-distinct-direction-sharpness/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/fstar-distinct-direction-sharpness
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/fstar-distinct-direction-sharpness --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Both direct modes report `PASS_DISTINCT_DIRECTION_SHARPNESS`: 30 family fixtures, 48,510 exact entry identities, all 2,592 local label/order cases, six independent ordered-block subset-DP optima, fifteen controls and two authenticated inputs. Each registered command took less than one second locally and has a 120-second bound. Registered replay reports `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

Committed bytes/modes and source ancestry pass at `a18fbc609be35ff15e5fd132a11ef6b36e9c1b0c`. Official export integrity and declared-input coverage pass for eight package/input files. Normal and optimized replay pass from the read-only Git-free export with empty PATH; all nine export files including its manifest retain their bytes and modes. Actual source-byte and inverse-sign corruptions reject in both modes, four rejecting executions. Optional generated receipts bind results to package hashes and source pins; no receipt is hand-written or committed.

To reproduce elsewhere, use the local CPython 3.12 executable in place of the absolute path above. `PROOF.md` supplies the all-positive-`k,s` argument; the executable caps its finite corroboration at `k<=10,s<=3`. Finite checks do not formally certify the universal proof.

## Limitations

No upper bound on the full F-star certificate or actual COPY cost is claimed. The universal twelve-line floor, physical/native realization, dirty restoration, full paid/target invoice and supplier admission remain open. The selected construction and its five framework assumptions are unchanged. Selected scientific cold replay, Lean/formal proof-kernel checking and independent human review were not run.

## Open next questions

- Prove the rational twelve-line floor eight or exhibit a literal box counterexample, distinguishing it from failure of the sufficient two-block route. Start with #3445's all-even remainder.
- Evaluate a stronger decoder certificate on the explicit `k=4` family while retaining its actual factors and original anchors. An actual cost theorem and complete physical invoice are still required.

## Related open work

Related work was refreshed after CI completion against newer open contributions. No additional PR studying this rational directed-box quantity was identified in the inspected scopes.

- [#2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717) studies general F-star structural certificates; this construction gives an exact sub-anchor box, without a full-certificate upper bound.
- [#2747](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2747) studies tied-line anchor/repair/pivot mixtures; this family has canonical tie size two and a separately proved box value.
- [#2774](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2774) studies zero digraphs and matched pivots; the new sparse-zero family is explicit, with no replay of its census.
- [#2890](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2890) studies higher-chromatic zero digraphs; this construction concerns a different supplied zero pattern and does not validate that PR's lemmas.
- [#2901](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2901) studies cancellation lines and insertion mixtures; all new family members have even canonical ties, with an exact box proof.
- [#2914](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2914) supplies the directed sub-anchor-box framework; this is a new sharp family in that framework.
- [#2936](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2936) studies fixture sub-decoders and box completeness; the present factors are a different explicit family.
- [#2963](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2963) studies eleven-line tied-minimum sub-decoders; none is recomputed or checked here.
- [#2978](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2978) supplies the credited rational core and triangular-rank bound; the new basis changes remove repeated directions while preserving sharpness.
- [#3012](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3012) studies box floors and the nonempty-tie restriction; every member here retains nonempty ties and its original global anchors.
- [#3031](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3031) studies the five-line box floor and shareable-class remainder; this construction concerns a new distinct-direction family, without auditing its conclusions.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated research package. Six new files only; frozen sources and shared code are untouched.
